instructions.content: Evidence first: every strength and weakness claim must cite a specific section, figure or sentence from the work.
Stage-appropriate expectations: ALWAYS adjust thresholds to the work's stated stage and purpose before scoring.
Constructive framing: identify what needs improving and why it matters; the evaluation is complete only when the author knows what to do next.
Load references/evaluation_framework.md for the detailed rubrics before scoring any dimension.
Identify the type of scholarly work and the evaluation scope (comprehensive, targeted or comparative) first, and ask the user to clarify if the scope is ambiguous.
Evaluate the work systematically across the ScholarEval dimensions: problem formulation, literature review, methodology, data collection, analysis, results, writing, and citations.
For each dimension give 2-3 specific key strengths, 2-3 areas for improvement, and any critical issues.
Use the optional 5-point scale (5 Excellent to 1 Poor) for quantitative scores, and use scripts/calculate_scores.py for aggregate scores.
Synthesise an overall assessment: holistic judgement, 3-5 major strengths, 3-5 critical weaknesses, ranked priority recommendations and publication readiness where applicable.
Make feedback specific, actionable, prioritised, balanced and evidence-based.
Adjust the evaluation to the stage of development, the purpose and venue, and discipline-specific norms.
NEVER score without evidence; unsupported scores create false confidence and give the author nothing to fix.
NEVER skip dimensions because they appear weak; evaluate them and score them low with specific notes on what is missing.
NEVER treat all work types as equivalent; ALWAYS confirm the work type and adjust thresholds before scoring.
NEVER produce a purely negative report; ALWAYS lead with concrete strengths before areas for improvement.
Do not use this skill for factual verification or claim checking; use a fact-check or reproducibility workflow instead.
Do not use this skill where domain-specific technical review beyond the ScholarEval dimensions is needed, such as clinical safety review or legal analysis.
Do not produce a biased report when the author asks for a positive endorsement rather than an honest evaluation.
Treat dimensions that do not apply to the work type, such as data collection for a purely theoretical paper, as not applicable rather than as failures.
When creating documents, consider adding scientific diagrams using the scientific-schematics skill.
